t:
Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating shall provide a report to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives on opportunities for cost savings and operational efficiencies that can be achieved through and the feasibility of colocating Coast Guard assets and personnel at facilities of other armed forces throughout the United States. The report shall—
    (1) identify opportunities for cooperative agreements with respect to siting of assets or operations that may be established between the Coast Guard and any of the other armed forces; and 
    (2) analyze anticipated costs and benefits, and operational impacts associated with each site and such agreements.

fable.w: The section only requires a report to congressional committees about colocating Coast Guard assets with other armed forces. The tempting reading treats the report and the "cooperative agreements" as participation, but Congress and the other armed forces are all inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, and no rulemaking, hearing or right to sue is created.
fable.s: shall provide a report to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives

opus.w: This section only requires a report to congressional committees, and Congress is part of the federal government. The "cooperative agreements" it mentions are between the Coast Guard and the other armed forces, so all of that coordination stays inside the government. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public takes part in any decision, so the tempting reading based on the word "cooperative" fails.
opus.s: identify opportunities for cooperative agreements with respect to siting of assets or operations that may be established between the Coast Guard and any of the other armed forces
opus.b: Someone might read "cooperative agreements" as participation, but that reading doesn't hold up. The only parties named are the Coast Guard and the other armed forces, and they're all part of the federal government. The report itself goes to congressional committees, which are also inside the government.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary to submit a report to congressional committees. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is an internal government action, not participation with outside parties. The analysis of cooperative agreements with other armed forces is also intra-governmental coordination.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating shall provide a report to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the report analyzes "cooperative agreements" with other armed forces, it involves coordination. However, the other armed forces are part of the federal government, so this is intra-governmental coordination, not participation with outside parties. Furthermore, the primary action is a report to Congress, which is also inside the federal government.
